PlotToLogbook.description:
One image on its way to the scan logbook, from one of two sources.

``image``: a rendered plot as a data URL rather than multipart form
data — the page already holds one (``Plotly.toImage`` returns it)
and form parsing would pull in ``python-multipart``, which this
package does not otherwise need. Base64 costs a third in size, which
a plot PNG can afford.

``path``: an artifact an analysis run produced, named as the run
listing names it (relative to ``analysis/ScanNNN/``). The portal
reads it off the share itself, under the artifact route's
containment rule, so a client that has only a reference — the MCP
server posting an agent's figures — never moves image bytes.
Exactly one of the two is given.
PlotToLogbook.title: PlotToLogbook

get.description: Redirect to today's day view.

Every loadable diagnostic and group in the configured tree, scan-free.

The per-run listing (below) is scoped to one scan; a client planning
what to run — an agent choosing an analyzer, or a page's picker —
needs the catalog before it has a scan. Same feature gate as the
runs; same loadable set as the per-run listing (``processing_infos``,
invalid YAMLs dropped). A group is listed with its resolved members
in run order, through ScanAnalysis's own loader — the portal runs one
diagnostic per job, so a group is a plan the caller expands, never
something this route runs.
The day page as JSON: its runs (newest first), filtered.
The day steppers' target as JSON (see :func:`run_jump`).

One run as JSON: the rail, the Overview tab and the device list.

``metadata`` is the Overview table verbatim (``metadata_rows``);
``devices`` are the image device folders (their tier is the
separate ``/device`` probe — one listing per device); the
neighbours and ``day_runs`` are the scan steppers and dropdown;
``analysis_enabled`` says whether the page offers the Analysis
tab (same gate as the template).

The scan's analyzers: applicability, job record, files on disk.

``applicable`` = the diagnostic's data device (``scan.device``,
else its name) has a data folder in this scan. Every loadable
diagnostic is listed regardless, so a device-less one is still
reachable; the tab collapses the inapplicable ones.

post.description:
Start one analyzer on this scan (202 + the fresh job record).

Ladder: feature off / extra missing 404 · unknown or unloadable
diagnostic 404 · folder unresolvable 404 · a destructive kind
without ``confirm=<this scan's number>`` 400 (the tab asks for
it; the gate is here so no client runs a delete unasked) · a job
already running for this scan 409 (its record in the body).
Build + run + cleanup happen on the worker thread, so everything
past this point — config errors included — lands in the record
as ``failed``.

get.description:
Per-bin membership for the Images tab's averaged grid.

The JSON carries the numbers (bins, counts, member shots — all
notebook-reproducible via the snippet); the pixels are served
by ``/run/{uid}/bin-image.png?bin=<index>`` per bin, so the
grid lazy-loads exactly like the per-shot gallery.

Per-bin centers + error bands + the ready binned figure.

Bins GROUP the data (``bincfg.bin_col``); the selected ``x``
PLACES it — each bin plots at the per-bin mean of the X column
(the owner's ruling: real scan-parameter positions now, x error
bars maybe later).  No ``x`` keeps the bin labels as the axis.
The union pick list: every plottable column with provenance.

One device's gallery tier — what clicking its name decides.

Same ``device_kind`` probe as the page (one directory listing,
no pixel reads), so the JSON and the Images tab can never
disagree about whether a device renders.
Live pass count for the filters popup: ``{pass, total}``.
Per-shot series + the ready figure for the selection.
Two-axis geometry, filtered scalar statistics and paired figures.

post.description:
Put one image — a rendered plot, or a run's artifact — into this scan's entry.

The portal's **third** write verb (after the analysis runs and the
config editor) and, like them, an explicit act: nothing is sent
that a person (or, through the MCP server, an agent) did not ask
for.  It writes to the logbook's own service through that service's
public API, and touches neither the scans tree nor any portal state
(an artifact source is READ off the analysis tree, nothing more).

Ladder: no absolute ``--logbook-url`` / not this experiment / no
scan number or day → 404 (there is no entry for it to join) · a
malformed image → 400 · an artifact path that does not resolve →
404, one that is not a raster image → 400 · the logbook unreachable
→ 503 · the logbook refusing → its own status for the verdicts that
are about this payload (409/413/415, and 404 for an ``entry_required``
entry that is gone — never a fresh one), else 502.  The reply carries
the attachment ``link`` the body now shows, so a caller appending
more can cite it.

get.description:
One shot of an ARRAY capture stack as a server-authored figure.

The line twin of ``/run/{uid}/image.png``.  A camera shot is
served as a rendered PNG because a 2048² frame as JSON is
absurd; a scope trace is a few thousand numbers and wants the
hover readout, so it travels as figure JSON like every other
plot here.  Same refusals as the image endpoint: a shot beyond
the recorded events, and a device that missed the shot, both
404 rather than serving a neighbour's trace.
The run list for one day (newest first, as the catalog lists).
The day/experiment picker form's target: redirect to the day view.
Liveness + catalog probe (the fleet-map health check) + version.

Day-step from the scan page without losing the analysis.

Redirects to the target day's run with scan number *prefer*
(else its newest run), carrying every other query param through
verbatim — the rail's day steppers point here so filters,
columns, and tab survive the hop.  A day with no runs falls
back to the day page.

One run: the rail + tabs (Overview / Plot / Images).

``tab``/``filters``/``bincfg``/``view``/``y``/``x`` are the
analysis-tab state, carried in the URL (statelessness doctrine:
a link IS the analysis) and consumed by the page's JS — the
server only threads them through the sticky query so steppers
keep the whole setup.

Serve one file a run produced, from the scan's analysis folder only.

Containment is the contract (:func:`analysis_runs.contained_artifact`):
anything that resolves outside the scan's own analysis folder is
a 404, same as a missing file. Same feature gate as the run
endpoints. Raster images render inline; every other type is a
download (``attachment`` + ``nosniff``) — the share is writable
by many hands, and a planted HTML/SVG must never execute in the
portal's (or, behind the OSPREY proxy, OSPREY's) origin.
``no-cache``: re-runs overwrite by name.

One bin's ``nanmean``-averaged device image, display-rendered.

``bin`` is the bin's INDEX in ``/api/.../bin-images`` order
(same ``_bin_groups`` call, so the two always agree). Member
shots that resolve to pixels are averaged (``average_frames``)
and windowed once; shots the device missed (no timestamp) or
that fail to load are skipped — the JSON's ``count`` is the
membership, the pixels are what actually loaded. With
``processing``, each member is ephemeral-processed FIRST and
the processed images average (process-then-average — the
correct order for nonlinear pipeline steps like thresholding).

One device shot rendered for display (stack or native file).

``processing`` names a diagnostic to run ephemerally on the
loaded pixels first (its ``processed_image`` renders instead of
the raw frame) — the write-free seam; raw serving is untouched
when the param is absent. ``display`` carries the image
cosmetics (``cmap`` + ``plo``/``phi`` window — types 400,
values degrade, per the display doctrine).

Server-rendered scalar plot: *y* column vs *x* (default row index).

Uses the matplotlib object API (``Figure``, never pyplot) — no
global figure registry, safe on FastAPI's threadpool.
